candidate_targets: those prone to automatic or autopilot behavior
original_extraction.evidence_text:
Take six slow, deep breaths. For the first three breaths, focus on your chest and abdomen; connect
with your breathing. For the next three breaths, expand your focus, so that as well as being aware of
your beathing, you’re also connecting fully with your environment; that is, while noticing your
breathing, also notice what you can see, hear, touch, taste and smell. Ready? Put the book down and
give it a go.
Er

---

What did you notice? Most people report that they feel far more “‘present-—more connected with
where they are and what they’re doing. Now, here’s another variation on the exercise. Again, read
the instructions first before trying it.

---

This time take nine slow, deep breaths. For the first three breaths, focus on your breathing. For the
next three breaths, focus on your breathing and also notice what thoughts are running through your

---

mind. (Whatever they are, just let them be.) For the final three breaths, focus on your breathing and
also scan your body and notice what you can feel. (Whatever you feel, just make room for it.) Okay.
Put the book down and give it a go.
rer

---

This variation on the exercise gives you a rapid way to increase self-awareness, accept what you’re
feeling and thinking, and gather your wits so you’re not on autopilot.

---

Now, here’s one more variation, which requires twelve breaths. This is the most important of all
these breathing exercises, so don’t skip it.
generation_rules: Begin with a set number of slow, deep breaths
Gradually expand focus from breathing to environment, thoughts, and bodily sensations
Encourage non-judgmental observation and acceptance of internal experiences
pause_rules: Include natural pauses between instructions to allow practice
Encourage slow, deep breathing to create space for observation
original_extraction.psychological_function: Promote mindfulness, self-awareness, emotional acceptance, and grounding in the present experience.
repetition_rules: Use sets of breaths divided into stages (e.g., first three breaths focus on breathing, next three on environment/thoughts/body) to scaffold awareness
symbolic_elements: breathing as a connection to self and environment
original_extraction.therapeutic_function: Increase present-moment awareness and self-connection through focused breathing and sensory observation; enhance acceptance of thoughts and bodily sensations; reduce automatic, autopilot behavior.
voice_rules: Use calm, guiding, and encouraging tone
Invite experiential engagement by prompting to put the book down and practice
